recentItems.title: Tiger Woods gets 5-year license suspension in plea deal | ABS-CBN Sports
recentItems.description:
Tiger Woods will have his license suspended for five years after reaching a plea deal on Wednesday (September 2) related to his impaired-driving case.

The 15-times major champion, who initially pleaded not guilty, was present for the change-of-plea hearing when Judge Darren Steele said two five-year driver's license suspensions will run at the same time, one on a reckless driving charge and one on a careless driving citation.

"There are no exceptions. If you were to drive for any reason at all, you would go immediately back to jail," Steele told the court.

The 50-year-old Woods, who was also handed fines, has 30 days to appeal the ruling.

Woods, dressed in a dark suit and tie, arrived at the Martin County Courthouse seated in the front passenger seat of a black SUV and did not answer questions from the gathered reporters as he and girlfriend Vanessa Trump walked in and out of the building for the 8:30 a.m. ET (1230 GMT) change of plea hearing.

(Production: Pavithra George)

recentItems.title: Grateful Argentine fans bid farewell to 'greatest' Messi after retirement announcement
recentItems.description:
Argentine fans thanked Lionel Messi and celebrated his legacy on Monday (August 31) after the 39-year-old announced his retirement from international football.

Messi, who captained Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup and to the final of this year's tournament, said on Instagram that the decision was painful but that he had given everything he could to the national team.

“I saw Maradona; I saw many players, Kempes, but Lionel Messi is superlative. There’s no comparison,” Argentine fan Carlos Sciata said.

Messi is Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 207 games and 125 goals. His relationship with the national team was once marked by disappointment, including defeats in the 2014 World Cup final and two successive Copa America finals.

He won the Copa America in 2021 before leading Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022.

“Messi was for me the greatest as a player, and as a person, and his retirement makes me sad,” said another fan, Nestor.

Defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final denied Messi a second consecutive World Cup title and a fairytale ending to his international career.

For many Argentines, however, his legacy extends beyond his trophies.

“The most important thing Messi left behind was the fact of insisting, persisting, pursuing a dream, a goal, an objective,” fan Jose Aramburu said.

(Camera and Editing: Horacio Soria. Writing: Nicolas Misculin, Julien Pretot, Chiranjit Ojha. Production: Anna Portella)
